research_conclusion: Cost-robustness classification: COST_ROBUST (verified). The short-horizon momentum edge survives the repository's existing realistic transaction-cost model and a 2x conservative stress for lookback 3/5/10 on the collected 10-asset universe: the candidate's per-segment median log returns move by at most 0.001 (base) / 0.002 (2x) and every zero-cost positive REGIME_STABLE edge asset (6 at lookback 3/5, 5 at lookback 10) stays positive. The absolute robustness arises because the constant-dollar daily rebalance generates small trades (candidate commission ~$21k on $1M vs a +554% full-sample return). Critical methodological qualification: the repository's matched coin-flip null is turnover-asymmetric (its discrete {-1,0,+1} jumps pay ~29x the candidate's commission and turn negative at 2x cost), so the framework's candidate-minus-null comparison is confounded under costs and its edge-count preservation (6/6/6 and 5/6/6) is NOT valid cost-robustness evidence; a turnover-matched null is required to certify the edge against a fair cost-matched null. Independently verified (4 gates) and reproducible; no signal tuning, universe expansion, or leverage.
